title: Microsoft Teams: new content-sharing layouts for Teams events
summary: Hold: the briefing calls licensing the administrator's only lever even though it also documents event-creation policies. It also says the roadmap states no prerequisite besides licensing, overlooking the requirement for production-tool access. The roadmap facts, licensing category, admin paths and commands otherwise check out.

claims.claim: Attendees see the resulting layout rather than the production controls.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events up to 1k attendees controls whether users with the policy can create events with up to 1,000 attendees, such as webinars.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Events policies.
Select an existing policy or create a new one.
For events with up to 1,000 attendees, such as webinars, turn the Events up to 1k attendees toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowWebinars Disabled prevents organisers with the policy from creating events with up to 1,000 attendees.
claims.quote:
To prevent organizers with this policy from creating events with up to 1,000 attendees, run the following command:
Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowWebinars Disabled

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience controls whether users with the policy can create large-audience events, such as town halls.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Events policies.
Select an existing policy or create a new one.
For events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls, turn the Events optimized for a large audience toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled prevents organisers with the policy from creating events optimised for large audiences.
claims.quote:
To prevent organizers with this policy from creating events optimized for large audiences, run the following command:
Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled

claims.claim: Changing either event-creation policy setting to Off after scheduling prevents the user from running or starting the affected event.
claims.quote: If you change the value to Off after a user schedules an event, they can't run or start the event.

claims.claim: The AllowWebinars and AllowTownhalls settings control event creation, not layout selection.
claims.quote:
Controls whether users with this policy can create events with up to 1,000 attendees, such as webinars.
Controls whether users with this policy can create events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference describes the policy as still in preview.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows you to configure options for customizing Teams events experiences. Note that this policy is currently still in preview.

claims.claim: Plan for Teams meetings lists No control for administrators for Manage what attendees see in meetings.
claims.quote: | Manage what attendees see | No control | Can decide who to spotlight during a meeting. |

claims.claim: Licensing is the one lever an administrator holds.
claims.quote:
The licence is the one lever an administrator holds.
The two Events policies rows are the blunt controls that exist. They decide whether users with the policy can create events of each type, not which layout organisers see.
claims.fix: Replace 'The licence is the one lever an administrator holds.' with 'Licensing is one lever an administrator holds.' The existing controls table already explains the separate event-creation controls, verified at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/set-up-events.
